publicationDescription:
SVG import could discard visible children that override inherited fill or stroke opacity. Resolve inherited paint-opacity properties through the author cascade before deciding whether geometry is visible.

Reviewed follow-ups preserve valid cascade rollback, evaluate context-free typed CSS math, and retain valid variable- or attribute-containing winners. Values needing custom-property, environment or attribute substitution or layout use an explicit fully opaque approximation; fresh imports and replacements warn that source-hidden artwork may be included and advise resolving expressions in an SVG editor for exact visibility. Invalid nested var/env/attr syntax preserves lower valid declarations. Escaped important identifiers are recognized from decoded CSS tokens. Both import paths consume decoded paint-opacity attribute values exactly once, including XML-encoded typed attr syntax in the worker. Scalar functions reject unsupported numeric types even when the delegated library could reduce them to a number. Full custom-property/environment/attribute substitution, named cascade layers and browser layout remain outside this importer scope.

The reported intermediate Infinity/NaN regression did not reproduce against the pinned library and actual browser controls. The reported flex-unit ratio matches current Chrome rejection, although CSS Values4 and Grid2 differ on support; that limitation is explicit. The independently reproduced sign(fr) type escape is repaired and legitimate round/clamp keyword controls remain covered.

Three previously locked MIT CSSTools packages are runtime dependencies with selected/generated notices. Independent source review covers both parser paths, syntax controls, approximation warnings and publication source identity.

publicationDescription:
Valid concave helical pockets were rejected because their area centroid can lie outside the enclosing pocket. Validate the complete ring, including closing edges, with the existing segment-containment predicate. Reuse the existing boundary index to skip repeated full scans only where a conservatively padded edge box cannot contact the boundary; possible contacts retain complete interval checks.

Regressions cover concavity, closing-edge crossings, tangency, coincidence, disconnected rings, islands and dense separated rings. Independent differential controls preserve complete generated plans. In the bounded eight-ring, 2048-vertex benchmark, the first repair took about 2.38 seconds and the indexed version 1.12 seconds, matching the earlier 1.15-second baseline. A deterministic regression reduces full-boundary checks from 768 to 3 for separated rings. Contact-heavy cases and the existing entry search retain their previous worst-case work.

publicationDescription:
Imported G-code preview previously used the background project estimate. Capture timing with the imported source and its machine assumptions, then use that same timeline for the displayed ETA and playback. Feed changes and dwell intervals now affect the imported route consistently.

The reviewed follow-up preserves timing for supported exported dialect words and explicit incremental arc centers, places same-block G4 before movement, and reports non-finite estimates as unavailable while retaining geometry. Play resumes a paused final dwell; Restart resets an initial dwell even when the distance scrubber is already zero. Unsupported source syntax keeps an explicit geometry-only fallback.

Hosted CI exposed a render loop when inactive preview received a new scheduler callback each render. Clearing an already-empty route now preserves state identity for the same imported owner. The original three status-poll tests remain unchanged and pass; bounded regressions cover idle owner changes and exit/reentry without stale geometry.

Live route progress now counts same-block G4 dwell as complete when physical movement proves it has elapsed, without pre-crediting leading, future or trailing waits at stationary boundaries. ExecutablePlan v1 assembly projects dwell events to its existing kind/line/seconds contract; internal ordering metadata remains available to parser-based timing, and the exact G-code bytes and closed schema are unchanged.
